title: Multifunctional elastic interlayer replaces rigid intercell spacer and top plate
description: Deletes per-module rigid top plate, tie-rods and discrete foam spacers; one continuous interlayer roll replaces ~24 cut foam pads and stamped compression hardware. Fewer parts, fewer assembly stations, and the plate-to-cell thermal path improves so cooling-plate area (aluminium kg) can shrink. Baseline Western prismatic packs (Taycan J1, Q6 e-tron) locate cells in aluminium module frames with a foamed EPP cover plus a rigid top plate carrying compression. Proposal: adopt CATL Qilin's multifunctional elastic interlayer — a ~2-3 mm compressible silicone/ceramic-filled foam sheet laid between the vertical cell wall and the large cooling plate, replacing both the discrete PU spacer AND the module frame's stack-pressure hardware. The interlayer does four jobs: absorbs LFP/NMC breathing (up to ~0.3 mm/cell over life), maintains contact pressure to the cooling plate (thermal conductance held even as cells swell), electrically insulates, and acts as a fire barrier between cell face and plate.

Cell array is stacked directly to the pack wall for compression reaction.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes tie-rod torque station and foam-pad pick-place per module (~10-12 stations across pack). Replaces with a single interlayer lay-down/roll-lamination station. Cycle time drops as module sub-assembly disappears; scrap from mis-cut foam pads eliminated. Modest capex for a lamination fixture; net tooling reduction from deleted module frame dies.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Continuous sheet is a single poka-yoke'd lay-up vs 24 discrete pads (mis-place risk). Compression reacts against pack wall — no tie-rod access needed, freeing tool clearance. Part count drops ~30 pieces/pack. Serviceability: cells no longer individually removable, so trades against repair — acceptable for CTP.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes module compression hardware and discrete spacers while improving thermal contact
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€65/pack deleted hardware+foam + ~€25/pack aluminium plate downgauge = ~€90/pack × 100,000 × ~0.7 realization = €6.3M; upper bound at full realization ~€9M

ideaData.riskNotes: Interlayer must sustain thermal-runaway barrier duty under GB 38031-2025 (no propagation, no fire outside pack for 2h post-trigger via heater/nail). Validate contact-pressure retention after ISO 12405-4 vibration + 1500-cycle aging; risk is pressure decay opening thermal gap. Mitigate with ceramic-filled grade and DIC-measured swell budget.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline 800V packs (Q6 e-tron, EQE) mount prismatic cells vent-up with a top gas-collection plenum, and use the pack lid as a separate sealed floor member. Proposal: adopt Zeekr Golden Battery's sandwich integration with cell inversion — cells rotated so vent valves face the pack BOTTOM into a dedicated shallow venting cavity in the tray, while the structural top cover becomes an uninterrupted flat panel that IS the cabin floor. The 'sandwich' stacks (top structural cover / cell array on elastic interlayer / cooling plate / bottom vent cavity + tray) as bonded laminate. Physics: bottom venting directs the ~600-800°C runaway jet away from the passenger compartment and lets the tray's crash-crush zone double as the vent duct, so no separate top plenum, no lid penetrations for gas, and the top cover carries pure structural load (bending/shear as floor) without sealing-around-vents complexity. Series/parallel busbars route on the plate mid-plane, shortening high-current paths for 800V.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes plenum weld/bond station and lid vent-cutting+resealing operations. Adds a tray-bottom cavity form (absorbed into existing HPDC/stamp tooling revision). Flat top cover raises stamping yield and lowers press tonnage. Net station reduction ~3-4; sealing test simplified.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Flat top cover eliminates vent-hole tolerance stack and local sealing beads. Cell inversion is a fixture-orientation change, poka-yoke by keyed cell tray. Vent path is line-of-sight to bottom — no ducting assembly. Serviceability: bottom-access venting inspected without opening cabin floor.

Confirm ECE R100.03 crash retains bottom cavity integrity. Mitigate with mica/ceramic liner in vent cavity and drainage to atmosphere via one-way flaps.

Physics: LFP's intrinsic thermal stability (nail-safe, ~270°C onset vs ~210°C NMC) permits eliminating inter-cell fire barriers and packing blades edge-to-edge, so the array density itself becomes structure. The ~960 mm span replaces separate cross-members: bending load transfers through cell cases into body sills. 800V achieved by series-stringing more blades at lower per-cell Ah.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count collapses from hundreds (module frames, cross-members, fasteners) to blade array + two skins + adhesive. Blades self-jig in a honeycomb comb fixture (poka-yoke). Trade-off: no cell-level service — whole pack repair. Tolerance stack managed by adhesive gap-fill.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: module deletion ~€90/pack + cross-member+fastener deletion ~€45/pack = ~€135/pack × 100,000 = €13.5M; upper bound with tray downgauge ~€18M

ideaData.riskNotes: Structural pack must pass ECE R100.03 crush + pole side impact with cells as load path (cell case deformation limits). GB 38031-2025 propagation relies on LFP stability — validate nail/heater with edge-to-edge packing (no barrier). Fatigue of adhesive laminate under ISO 12405 vibration over life is the key durability risk; mitigate with structural epoxy + peel-stop features.

ideaData.title: Structural foam + adhesive bonds cylindrical array as pack shear panel
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: Western 46xx/2170 cylindrical concepts (BMW Gen6, Rivian R2) still locate cells in a plastic or aluminium honeycomb carrier then bolt a lid. Proposal: adopt Tesla 4680 structural-pack practice — flood the interstitial voids of a 46×95/46×120 cell array with a two-part structural PU/epoxy foam that simultaneously bonds each cell can to top and bottom skins, turning the filled array into a shear-carrying sandwich core. Physics: individually weak cell cans become collectively stiff when the cured foam couples them into a continuous core carrying in-plane shear between the two structural skins (like end-grain balsa). The foam is also the cell retention and the thermal-runaway isolation medium (limits cell-to-cell heat via low-k foam + intumescent additive). No carrier frame, no bolted lid-to-carrier interface. 800V realised via series busbar plates laser-welded to tabless cell ends before flooding.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Deletes honeycomb carrier and its fasteners; foam is retention + structure + thermal barrier in one dispense. Skins downgauge because the filled core adds shear stiffness. Fewer joints cut labour and warranty. Foam replaces separate potting AND spacers.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes carrier injection-mould/insert stations; adds a metered 2K foam dispense + cure station (existing tech). Requires dam/tooling for controlled flood and outgassing control. Net capex neutral-to-negative vs carrier tooling; cure time is the cycle-time constraint — mitigate with fast-cure chemistry.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count drops (no carrier, fewer fasteners). Cells self-locate in a temporary comb, flooded, cured — poka-yoke by fixture. Zero cell serviceability (destructive to remove) — pack-level exchange model. Tolerance absorbed by foam. Busbar access must precede flood.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Foam does structure, retention and fire barrier; carrier deleted
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: carrier+fastener deletion ~€70/pack + skin downgauge ~€20/pack + spacer/potting merge ~€15/pack = ~€105/pack × 100,000 ≈ €10.5M

ideaData.riskNotes: Foam must limit propagation per GB 38031-2025 (heater trigger, no cascade) — validate intumescent loading. Adhesion durability over -40/+60°C thermal cycling and ISO 12405 vibration is critical: bond-line fatigue could delaminate skins. Confirm structural contribution retained after ECE R100.03 crush. Mitigate with primer + peel-stop and DVP thermal-shock coupons.

How this differs: formulates the foam as combined retention+shear-core+intumescent barrier to also delete the carrier frame and downgauge skins, targeted at 800V series-string tabless arrays

benchmarkAnchor.difference: formulates the foam as combined retention+shear-core+intumescent barrier to also delete the carrier frame and downgauge skins, targeted at 800V series-string tabless arrays

Final assembly gains a marriage-line seal-and-torque station replacing pan weld cell. Net BIW weld-cell energy and station reduction.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Eliminates one large stamping and its weld flanges; single perimeter gasket poka-yoke'd on cover. Marriage sealing must be robust — CTB experience shows feasibility. Serviceability: pack drop requires cabin-floor removal path — plan hoist access. Tolerance: cover-to-sill flatness becomes a body datum.

ideaData.title: Series-blade 800V stringing shrinks parallel count and busbar copper
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: many 800V packs reach voltage by series-stacking ~100+ high-Ah prismatic cells with heavy parallel groups (e.g. 2-3P) needing thick copper busbars for the parallel current. Proposal: adopt Zeekr Golden / BYD short-blade topology — use lower-Ah (~40-60 Ah) short-blade LFP cells series-strung to ~800V with a 1P (or fewer-P) configuration. Physics: at fixed pack energy, more series cells at lower Ah means each string carries less current for the same power, so busbar cross-section (copper/aluminium kg) scales down (I²R and ampacity both ease). Fewer parallel joints eliminate inter-cell parallel welds. The short-blade format keeps the structural-rib benefit while the electrical topology cuts conductor mass. 4C-12C fast charge is enabled by short ion path in the thin blade, not by paralleling.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Lower per-string current lets busbar/interconnect copper cross-section shrink (material kg). Fewer parallel groups delete parallel-weld joints (labour + scrap). Thinner busbars ease insulation/creepage layout, reducing isolation-part complexity at 800V.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Fewer parallel welds per pack removes weld stations and cuts weld-scrap rework. Busbar stamping tonnage/material drops. More series joints add series-weld count — net depends on cell count; short-blade many-series still nets fewer parallel joints. Minor tooling change to thinner busbar dies.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Fewer parallel connections simplify busbar routing and creepage clearances at 800V (fewer high-current nodes). Thinner busbars easier to bend/route (DFA). Trade: more series cells to place — mitigated by blade comb fixture. Weld access unchanged.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Lower string current shrinks conductor mass and parallel joint count
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: busbar copper downgauge ~€25/pack + deleted parallel welds ~€20/pack + isolation simplification ~€8 = ~€53/pack × 100,000 ≈ €5.3M

ideaData.riskNotes: Higher series count raises single-cell-open failure sensitivity and cell-to-cell voltage matching burden on BMS — validate string balancing. 800V creepage/clearance must meet ECE R100.03 and IEC isolation with more nodes; validate partial-discharge. Fast-charge heat with 1P must not exceed thermal budget — confirm cooling under GB 38031 abuse and 4C DVP.

ideaData.title: Reuse rear drive unit as onboard boost-rectifier for 400V charging
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: 800V packs either accept slow 400V DC charging or add a dedicated DC-DC boost converter (cost, mass, packaging). Proposal: adopt Lucid Wunderbox / GM Ultium concept at the pack-architecture level — reuse the existing rear-drive-unit inverter and motor windings as a boost-rectifier so a 400V DC charger current is stepped up to the 800V pack, eliminating a standalone boost converter. Physics: the motor's stator inductance plus the inverter's switches form an interleaved boost stage (motor stationary, torque cancelled) — the same silicon/magnetics already in the powertrain do double duty. At the pack level this changes the HV bus architecture: the charge port routes through the drive-unit node rather than a dedicated converter, simplifying the HV junction box. Compatible with 2×400V bank-charge fallback (already in library) as a lower-cost alternative or complement.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Deletes a whole subassembly and its connectors (major part-count and joint reduction). Adds one contactor and control lines — simple DFA. Serviceability: charging fault diagnosis now spans drive unit + pack — document interlocks. Creepage layout in junction box eases with fewer nodes.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: single-layer skateboard 800V packs (Q6 e-tron, most) leave vehicle underfloor recesses (footwell/tunnel) unused, capping energy at ~72% volume utilisation. Proposal: adopt Porsche Taycan 'foot garage' two-layer architecture — stack a second cell layer only in the footwell recesses so rear-seat passengers' feet sit above a locally lower single layer while the front footwell region carries a double stack. Physics: pack energy = usable volume × volumetric density; exploiting non-rectangular cabin volume adds kWh without changing cell chemistry or format, improving $/kWh via fixed-cost amortisation (tray, BMS, contactors are per-pack, not per-kWh). ideaData.title: Standardised swap-envelope shell enables volume commonisation across models
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: each Western model gets a bespoke pack outline bolted uniquely to its body, so tooling, seals and BMS layouts are model-specific (low reuse). ideaData.dfmDfa: Frozen mounting/connector datums mean common fixtures and poka-yoke across models (huge DFA win). Variant complexity pushed inside the shell where it is cheaper to manage. ideaData.title: Rationalise to two shared aluminium extrusion profiles for tray frame
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline Western 800V trays (Taycan/PPE style) use 6-10 bespoke extruded profiles per pack (front rail, rear rail, two side sills, cross-members, sensor channel) in EN AW-6060-T6 / 6082-T6, each a separate die (~€30-60k tooling) with unique cut/miter/CNC end-machining fixtures. FSW corner joining at 4 corners; ~30% fewer weld metres. Two capex dies retired at next facelift; profile inventory SKUs cut ~70%.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~6 retired dies × €45k amortised over programme + extrusion price delta ~€0.15/kg on ~35 kg frame × 100k + SKU-carrying savings; ~€18-32/pack × 100k

ideaData.riskNotes: Universal profile is a compromise section; must re-validate side-pole intrusion and crush per ECE R100.03 mechanical shock and the crash load cases, plus enclosure IP67 seal integrity at re-designed corners. title: Gigacast-integrated rear pack mount deletes bracket cluster
description: Deletes 6-14 bracket parts + their fasteners + BIW welds + e-coat masking. Cast-in bosses add near-zero incremental casting cost (feature in existing die). Assembly stations for bracket weld/fit removed; torque operations reduced. Warranty reserve for joint loosening cut. Baseline packs bolt to body via 6-14 discrete stamped-steel/cast brackets and adapter plates welded to BIW, each a separate stamping/weld/coat part with its own fastener set. Proposal: exploit the front+rear gigacastings (as on Tesla structural pack and XPeng G6) by casting the pack-tray load-transfer bosses and threaded-insert nests directly into the AlSi7Mg0.3 (AlSi10MnMg-class) rear gigacasting, so the tray perimeter bolts straight into cast-in bosses with helical inserts, deleting the bracket cluster. Cast bosses are net-shape with 1.5 mm machining stock on the mating face only. Physics: cast load paths route pack reaction into the node structure of the casting with shorter, stiffer load lines than bolted brackets

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline aluminium enclosures use a 2.5-3.0 mm 5xxx/6xxx tray floor plus a separate underbody skidplate, chosen for weight but costly per kg (Europe +56% cost region, aluminium premium). Proposal for cost-region-sensitive entry 800V LFP packs (BYD Blade philosophy tolerates a heavier, cheaper structure at ~150 Wh/kg): a single hot-formed 22MnB5 boron-steel floor (1.2-1.5 mm, ~1,500 MPa after press-hardening) that IS both the tray floor and the impact/skid shield. Deletes skidplate stamping/fit station. Requires cataphoretic corrosion protection line for steel. Cycle time set by furnace, mitigated by multi-cavity.

title: Structural-adhesive-bonded tray lid deletes 80% of perimeter bolts
description: Deletes ~50 bolts + weld-nuts/inserts + their torque cycle time; deletes the separate compressed gasket (adhesive doubles as seal); reduces flange width/material. Adds one adhesive-dispense + fixture-cure station. Net labour and BOM fall. Baseline pack lids (Taycan, PPE, EVA2) seal via a continuous EPDM/liquid gasket clamped by 40-70 M6 bolts on a flanged perimeter, each bolt a torque op + a leak/creepage path. title: Two-layer footwell-recess tray reused across two wheelbases
description: One tooled core amortised across two-plus vehicle lines instead of two bespoke trays; only the small recess sub-tray varies. Cuts perimeter/floor die count and validation duplication. Sourcing volume on the common core lowers piece price. Baseline: each wheelbase gets a bespoke single-depth tray, forcing new perimeter tooling per model. Proposal borrows Taycan's two-layer 'foot garage' recess concept but as a commonisation lever: a common central deep-well tray module (fixed footprint, houses the primary blade/prismatic array) plus a bolt-on second-layer footwell-recess sub-tray whose presence/absence and length flexes capacity and wheelbase. Physics/packaging: decoupling capacity into a fixed core + modular recess lets one tooled core serve short and long wheelbases, and the recessed second layer recovers cabin footroom without new central tooling. The interface is a machined, gasket-sealed flange between core and recess sub-tray.

title: Underbody ballistic liner as tray floor rather than bolt-on plate
description: Deletes the bolt-on skidplate part, its ~15-25 fasteners and perimeter attach frame; lower areal mass than a steel skid saves weight (range/energy credit). Co-bond is one lamination op vs a separate stamped/moulded plate line. Baseline: aluminium/steel tray floor PLUS a separate bolted underbody protection plate (steel or composite) with an air gap, adding a part, fasteners and mass. Proposal: laminate a thin UHMWPE/aramid ballistic-grade skin (or a thermoplastic composite armour layer, ~2-3 mm) directly onto the underside of the tray floor as a co-bonded sacrificial impact/anti-intrusion liner, replacing the discrete skidplate. Physics: high-tenacity fibre distributes and arrests a stone/road-debris impact energy over a wide area (like soft-armour), preventing floor puncture at far lower areal mass than a steel plate; bonding it to the floor removes the air-gap fasteners and the standalone plate's own perimeter frame. The tray floor + liner become one impact-managed laminate.

ideaData.title: Elastic interlayer inter-cell plate replaces bottom cold plate
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: 400V-legacy prismatic pack (EVA2/PPE style) with one bottom AA3003 cold plate under the module stack plus a thermally-conductive gap filler (~2.5 W/mK, 2-3 mm) bridging cell base to plate. Proposal: adopt Qilin-style large water-cooling plates BETWEEN every cell pair — a 1.2 mm roll-bonded AA3003 microchannel sheet stood vertically in the cell gap combined with a multifunctional elastic (silicone-foam) interlayer that provides both stack-pressure compliance and the vent/thermal barrier. Cooling area rises ~4× because the whole 960 mm x cell-height flank is wetted rather than the ~thin base. The physics: with LFP/NMC the dominant thermal gradient is along the electrode stack; side cooling shortens the conduction path to ~½ cell thickness (~12-14 mm) instead of full cell height (~100 mm), so peak-to-mean cell ΔT during 4C drops enough to delete the bottom plate and its gap filler entirely.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Deleting the full bottom cold plate (large brazed/roll-bonded sheet) and the m2-scale gap-filler bead removes the single largest thermal BOM line and its dispense station. Inter-cell plates are thin, high-yield roll-bond and double as compression members, so the mechanical spacer set also shrinks.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes one large cold-plate braze/assembly line and the bottom gap-filler dispense+cure station (high-cost 2-part material, robot, cure oven). Adds automated insertion of thin inter-cell plates during stack build — folded into existing stacking cell, ~+2 s/cell. Net station count down; plant capex for the gap-filler cell (~€1.5-2M) avoided.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part-count: 1 large plate + gap-filler bead deleted; N/2 thin plates added but they self-locate in the elastic interlayer (poka-yoke slot), no separate fixture. Serviceability worsens (plates internal to stack) so pack becomes non-serviceable-at-cell — acceptable for CTP. Tolerance stack governed by interlayer compression set, not braze flatness.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes the highest-cost single thermal component (bottom plate) plus a major consumable (gap filler) while improving fast-charge thermal margin.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €3-5/kWh x 90 kWh x 100,000 = €27M-€45M; add ~€2M/yr avoided gap-filler consumable (0.6 kg/pack x €30/kg x 100k).

ideaData.riskNotes: Vertical inter-cell plates sit in the vent path; a plate breach could route hot gas into coolant. Must pass GB 38031-2025 thermal propagation (no fire/no cabin breach 5 min→2h) and coolant-into-cell leak test. Mitigate with the elastic interlayer as an ablative barrier between cell wall and plate, and a burst-rated plate seam validated by heater-trigger propagation test.

How this differs: we use the side cooling to fully DELETE the bottom cold plate and its gap filler, not add it on top; targeted at a legacy Western prismatic pack rather than a clean-sheet CTP

title: Blade-flank contact cooling deletes inter-cell coolant plate
description: One shared under-array plate replaces one-plate-per-cell-group plus all inter-cell TIM; fewer coolant joints, fewer braze seams, less aluminium mass, and TIM consumable eliminated at architecture level. Baseline: prismatic-cell packs cool via a dedicated coolant plate at each thermal face plus TIM. Proposal: borrow BYD Blade geometry — 960 mm long, ~13-14 mm thin LFP cells laid flat — where the enormous flank area (960 x cell-height ≈ 0.12-0.15 m2 per cell) gives such a low surface-heat-flux that a single 2.0 mm roll-bonded AA3003 plate running UNDER the long flat array services many cells with no per-cell inter-plate. The physics: heat generation per unit cooled area falls with the huge blade footprint; even at 3C the flux is low enough that base conduction along the thin cell (thickness ~13 mm) keeps core ΔT within limits, so the multi-plate/TIM sandwich of short-cell packs is unnecessary.

title: TIM elimination via direct cell-can-to-plate solder wetting
description: Deletes the entire TIM consumable and its 2-part dispense/cure line; the solder mass is tiny by comparison. Improved thermal path lets plate wall downgauge, saving aluminium. Removes gap-filler warranty risk (pump-out, voids). Baseline: prismatic/cylindrical cells bridge to the cold plate through a 1.5-3 mm thermally-conductive gap filler (2-3 W/mK) that costs both material and a dispense/cure line. Proposal: at architecture level, replace the gap filler with a low-temperature (Sn-Bi ~139 °C eutectic) solderable interface: cell can base is Ni-flashed, cold-plate top face is pre-tinned, and reflow at ~155 °C bonds every can directly to the plate (~0.1 mm bondline, ~50 W/mK). The physics: interfacial thermal resistance drops ~20-30x versus polymer TIM because a metallurgical joint removes the polymer's low conductivity and eliminates the air-gap-filling thickness margin; core-to-coolant ΔT falls, enabling either faster charge or thinner plate.

ideaData.title: TIM elimination via direct cell-can-to-plate solder wetting
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: prismatic/cylindrical cells bridge to the cold plate through a 1.5-3 mm thermally-conductive gap filler (2-3 W/mK) that costs both material and a dispense/cure line. Proposal: at architecture level, replace the gap filler with a low-temperature (Sn-Bi ~139 °C eutectic) solderable interface: cell can base is Ni-flashed, cold-plate top face is pre-tinned, and reflow at ~155 °C bonds every can directly to the plate (~0.1 mm bondline, ~50 W/mK). The physics: interfacial thermal resistance drops ~20-30x versus polymer TIM because a metallurgical joint removes the polymer's low conductivity and eliminates the air-gap-filling thickness margin; core-to-coolant ΔT falls, enabling either faster charge or thinner plate.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Deletes the entire TIM consumable and its 2-part dispense/cure line; the solder mass is tiny by comparison. Improved thermal path lets plate wall downgauge, saving aluminium. Removes gap-filler warranty risk (pump-out, voids).
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes TIM dispense robot + cure oven (~€2M line). Adds a controlled reflow pass over the plate/cell interface — a pass-through IR/hot-plate station gated below cell max temp. Cycle governed by reflow dwell (~60-90 s), offset by removing cure. Flux-clean step added.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Single-sided assembly; cans self-locate on solder-mask-defined pads (poka-yoke). Rework = local induction de-solder, so partial serviceability retained (better than potting). Tolerance stack tightened to plate flatness + can flatness, no compliant TIM to absorb gaps — needs plate flatness ≤0.3 mm.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates a costly, warranty-prone consumable and improves fast-charge margin.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: TIM ~€2.5/kWh (0.8 kg x €28/kg + dispense) + €0.5-1/kWh plate downgauge; x 90 kWh x 100k.

ideaData.riskNotes: Sn-Bi is brittle; thermal-cycle fatigue of the joint under charge/discharge ΔT must survive ISO 12405 vibration + thermal cycling. title: Bank-split thermal zoning enables half-pack cooling at low load
description: Reuses the existing bank-split electrical partition to zone the coolant with two low-cost valves, cutting parasitic pump energy (range/efficiency win) and allowing a smaller pump than a single always-full-flow loop. Baseline: 800V packs cool the entire cell array continuously; the coolant loop and pump serve all cells even when only part of the pack is thermally stressed. Proposal: exploit the bank-charge topology (PPE/GM Ultium split into two 400V halves) to also SPLIT the coolant circuit into two independently-valved zones. During DC fast charge both zones flow; during cruise or the tapered charge tail, one zone's flow is shut and its pump duty drops — pumping only the actively-heated half. The physics: parasitic pump power scales with flow cubed against system resistance; halving served volume at partial load cuts pump energy disproportionately, and matching flow to actual per-zone heat avoids overcooling one half.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Leverages existing bank-split boundary as the coolant divide (natural datum). +2 valves, -pump-size. Serviceability: valves manifold-mounted, accessible. Poka-yoke keyed valve ports.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Part-count halved per gap; single insertion is poka-yoke'd by asymmetric thickness (foam side faces one cell). Tolerance stack simplified — one compressible part governs gap. Serviceability unchanged (internal).

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: two parts + two placements ~€4/kWh vs one laminate + one placement ~€2/kWh = €1.5-2.5/kWh saved x 90 x 100k.

ideaData.riskNotes: Combined part must still pass GB 38031-2025 no-propagation with heater/nail trigger — validate the intumescent char forms before neighbour reaches onset, and that foam degradation at high T doesn't compromise the barrier. title: Self-draining channel-less floor plate: coolant path is the tray
description: Eliminates the separate cold plate, the plate-to-tray adhesive/sealant and that leak interface; the floor performs structure + cooling. Removes one large braze/bond operation and its leak-test, and cuts aluminium (one sheet set does both jobs). Baseline: pack tray and cold plate are separate assemblies — an HPDC/stamped tray plus a brazed microchannel cold plate bonded on top with sealant, adding a part, a joint and a leak interface. Proposal (distinct from HPDC-manifold-in-tray): a friction-stir-welded twin-sheet floor where two 1.5 mm AA5754 sheets are FSW'd around pre-formed inflated channels (roll-bond-then-inflate) so the STRUCTURAL floor sheet IS the cooling circuit — no separate plate, no bonding sealant, cells sit directly on the upper sheet. The physics: hydro-inflated roll-bond channels give continuous coolant contact under the full cell footprint with the structural sheet as one wall, so conduction path is one sheet thickness (~1.5 mm) with no adhesive thermal resistance.

title: Cell-inversion bottom-vented array simplifies HV isolation routing
description: Cleaner top plane allows tighter busbar/CCS spacing (less copper span, smaller FPC), deletes local vent-gas isolation shrouds around HV connectors, and reduces conformal-coat/potting used to survive effluent contamination on the electrical plane. Baseline: top-vented cells route thermal-runaway gas past busbars, sense FPC and HV connectors on the top plane, forcing extra isolation, gas barriers and creepage margin around live electrical hardware near the vent path. Proposal: invert cells to vent downward into a dedicated bottom plenum (Zeekr Golden Battery / bottom-venting practice), keeping the entire top electrical plane — busbars, CCS FPC, BDU, connectors — away from hot conductive vent gas. Physics: conductive runaway effluent is the main cause of secondary arc/short between HV nodes; separating the vent path from the electrical plane lets creepage/clearance be set by steady-state 800V, not by contamination-derated distances, shrinking busbar spacing and deleting local gas shields

ideaData.title: Dry-electrode coating line deletes NMP recovery and drying oven
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: NMC811 cathode slurry-cast with NMP solvent onto Al foil, then a 60-100 m gas-fired drying oven and a full NMP solvent-recovery/condensation plant (distillation columns, chillers, activated-carbon beds) — the drying/solvent block is 30-40% of electrode-line capex and a major kWh/kWh energy line item. Physics: PTFE shear-fibrillates into a 3D fibril web that mechanically entraps active particles, so binder migration on drying (which drives adhesion loss and rate fade in wet coating) simply cannot occur; film is denser (higher volumetric loading) so fewer metres of coated foil per kWh.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes ~80 m of drying oven and the entire NMP condensation/distillation island (2-4 stations + tank farm). Adds a powder-mixing/fibrillation station and a heated calender nip. Net footprint down ~25-35% on the electrode line; plant gas load drops sharply. Calender line speed becomes the takt constraint; scrap film re-fed to mixer.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Fewer process stations, fewer utility tie-ins (no solvent pipe runs, no vapour-abatement). Film-on-foil handling needs new web-tension control (self-supporting film is more tear-prone at <60 µm). Poka-yoke: inline film-thickness beta gauge rejects out-of-spec before winding. Serviceability unaffected — cell-level change.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Solvent plant and oven are among the largest single capex/energy blocks in cell making; removing them compounds across every kWh built.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 6 GWh × ~$4-6/kWh drying+solvent+energy delta × ~€0.92/$ ≈ €22M-€33M energy/consumable + ~€8-20M/yr avoided capex amortisation on the deleted oven/recovery island

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline (Taycan/Audi PPE/Mercedes EVA2 legacy 800V): prismatic NMC cells are framed into 10-33 modules, each with end plates, tie-rods/banding, module busbars, module BMS slave, module cooling interface and module-to-tray fasteners — the module sub-line is 20-30 assembly stations and drives part count into the thousands. Physics: the long-cell aspect ratio lets the cell body itself carry compression and vent bottom-out, and large-area side cooling replaces per-module cold-plate interfaces.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes the module sub-line and its stations/robots; replaces with a cell-stacking + interlayer-lay-up + tray-insertion cell that has far fewer stations at higher takt. ideaData.dfmDfa: Massive part-count reduction (thousands of module fasteners/frames deleted). Stack-pressure now reacted by pack walls — wall stiffness and tolerance stack become critical; poka-yoke via a calibrated compression fixture at insertion. Serviceability trade: bonded/compressed array is less field-repairable — accept for volume trims, keep modular for repair-priority trims (Audi-style).

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€8/kWh avg pack-level saving × 90 kWh × 100,000 packs = ~€72M; range reflects module-content variance vs the specific legacy baseline replaced

ideaData.riskNotes: Losing module firebreaks concentrates propagation risk on the interlayer + bottom-venting design; must pass GB 38031-2025 no-fire-no-explosion propagation and ECE R100.03. Mitigate with mica/aerogel interlayer, bottom vent channel, and validated wall-preload spec.

title: Debondable structural adhesive keeps CTP pack field-serviceable
description: Keeps CTP's station-count and structural-mass savings while collapsing the warranty reserve for single-cell repair (repair vs whole-pack scrap). Enables EOL cell harvesting/second-life recovery, raising residual value. Same adhesive dispense station — no added assembly cost. Baseline: structural cell-to-tray bonding (Tesla-style) uses permanent 2K PU/epoxy or structural foam — excellent stiffness and station count, but the pack is effectively non-repairable, forcing whole-pack swap on a single-cell fault (large warranty reserve). Legacy modular packs stay serviceable but carry the module cost. title: EOL leak test by helium tracer batches out multi-pack chambers
description: Cuts per-pack leak-test cycle time from minutes to seconds, deleting redundant parallel decay stations (station capex + floorspace + operators). Higher sensitivity cuts false-reject rework and, critically, field-escape warranty from missed micro-leaks that decay tests miss. Baseline: each finished pack gets an individual air-decay/pressure-decay leak test (IP67/IP6K9K seal integrity) at an EOL station — long dwell (minutes) per pack due to thermal-settling of trapped air, making leak test a takt bottleneck that forces parallel test stations. Proposal: switch to helium tracer-gas leak testing in a batched vacuum-hood arrangement — pack backfilled with a 5-10% He/air trace, placed in a hood, He detected by mass spectrometer sniffer/accumulation. Physics: helium's small molecule and mass-spec sensitivity (down to ~1e-6 mbar·L/s) resolve a leak in seconds regardless of ambient temperature drift, versus pressure-decay's minutes-long settling — decoupling test time from thermal noise. ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cells are placed one-by-one into the tray by vision-guided 6-axis robots referencing datum pins, with returnable dunnage feeding cells and a gantry indexing each placement — a slow, capex-heavy stacking sub-line whose takt is bounded by placement cycles and vision cycle time. Physics: with long blade/short cells the aspect ratio makes a stacked stick self-aligning against the tray's V-ribs (kinematic seating); stack pressure from the comb keeps geometry stable so one insertion replaces dozens of pick-place cycles.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Replaces per-cell robotic pick-and-place with single-stroke stick insertion → fewer robots/gantries (capex) and dramatically shorter stacking takt (fewer parallel stations). ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes multiple vision-guided placement robots and their controllers; adds a stick-forming (comb load) upstream cell and a single-stroke insertion press. Tray gets integral V-ribs (tooling change). Big drop in stacking-station count and takt; conveyance simplified to stick handling.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part-count neutral on product but massive station reduction. Tray locating ribs act as poka-yoke — a mis-oriented stick won't seat. Tolerance stack shifts from robot-repeatability to rib+comb tolerance (tighten tray rib machining). Serviceability: reusable comb allows extraction of a stick for repair.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Attacks the stacking sub-line's robot capex and takt, the pacing item in many pack lines.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3/kWh × 90 kWh × 100,000 = ~€27M from deleted placement robots (capex amortisation), reduced parallel stations from faster takt, and dunnage-to-reusable-comb conversion

ideaData.riskNotes: Single-stroke insertion risks cell-edge scuffing/insulation damage and uneven seating → creepage/isolation faults (ECE R100.03 isolation resistance). Wall/rib-reacted stack pressure must survive ISO 12405 vibration. Mitigate: chamfered lead-in ribs, insertion force-monitoring with abort, and 100% post-insert isolation + gap-scan before bonding.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inspired by / benchmarked against: BYD Blade / CATL Qilin large-format cell stacking — handling long cells as a self-aligning compressed array inserted as a group rather than pick-placed individually. How this differs: Formalises a reusable-comb 'stick' + kinematic tray-rib self-datuming to delete vision-guided placement robots, framed as a stacking-takt and stacking-capex lever for an 800V line

ideaData.title: In-pack cell balancing at first charge deletes sorting/binning line
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cells are capacity/impedance graded and sorted into tight matched bins before pack assembly to minimise in-pack imbalance — grading + binning is an added test-and-logistics operation with WIP buffers per bin, and mismatched-bin inventory ties up capital. Proposal: skip fine binning; assemble packs from a broad tolerance band and let the pack's own active/passive balancing + a first-in-pack conditioning charge equalise the array, with the ML formation-signature (from the aging idea) used to pre-group only coarsely. Physics: modern LFP/NMC cell-to-cell variance is small enough that the balancing budget over pack life absorbs a wider intake band; the flat LFP OCV curve makes tight capacity matching less thermodynamically necessary than for high-slope chemistries, and the BMS balancing current recovers usable capacity that fine binning was protecting.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Deletes the grading/binning sub-line and its per-bin WIP buffers and inventory finance. Removes bin-mismatch scrap/downgrade. Reduces cell-logistics complexity (one intake stream vs many bins). Balancing hardware already present, so no added product cost.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes the binning station bank and multi-bin conveyance/storage; adds a first-in-pack conditioning-charge step at EOL (can piggyback on the existing EOL charge/functional test). Net station and floorspace reduction; simplified cell feed. Slightly longer EOL conditioning dwell.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Single cell intake stream is a large logistics simplification. Poka-yoke: coarse formation-signature gate blocks gross outliers from entering a pack. Serviceability: replacement cell need only be within the coarse band, easing spare-part stocking (commonisation of service cells).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes a whole test-and-logistics sub-line and its inventory finance where chemistry variance permits.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Deleted binning stations + per-bin WIP finance + bin-mismatch downgrade avoided, net of slightly longer EOL conditioning; strongest on LFP trims

ideaData.riskNotes: Wider intake band raises worst-case in-pack imbalance → uneven aging, reduced usable capacity and potential overcharge of the weak cell (safety/thermal exposure, GB 38031-2025). Mitigate: define the intake band from the proven balancing budget with margin; keep the coarse formation-signature outlier gate; validate over accelerated life that end-of-life imbalance stays within BMS authority.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inspired by / benchmarked against: BYD Blade LFP vertically-integrated cell-to-pack flow (minimal binning) vs legacy NMC tight-bin practice — exploiting LFP variance tolerance and vertical integration to minimise pre-assembly grading. How this differs: Ties the wider-band intake to the ML formation-signature coarse gate and an EOL in-pack conditioning charge, explicitly deleting the binning sub-line as a manufacturing-strategy lever

ideaData.title: Wire-bond cell interconnect replaces laser busbar welding stations
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cell-to-busbar interconnects are made by laser welding (or ultrasonic) at dedicated stations with fume extraction, weld-quality vision and high scrap sensitivity to gap/tolerance — welds are hard to rework and a bad weld can scrap a partly-built pack. Proposal: for cylindrical-format 800V packs (4695/46120 or 21700), use heavy-gauge aluminium wire-bonding (300-500 µm Al wire, ultrasonic wedge bond) to connect cell terminals to a flex/PCB collector, as used in some cylindrical packs. Physics: each wire bond is an individual fusible link — it acts as a per-cell fuse (opens on cell short), giving intrinsic single-cell isolation without separate fuse elements, while the ultrasonic wedge bond tolerates larger cell-height tolerance than a laser weld's tight focal gap, cutting fixturing precision cost.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Wire bonds provide integral per-cell fusing → deletes discrete cell fuse elements (BOM). Wedge bonding tolerates height variance → relaxes fixturing/tolerance cost and cuts weld-scrap of near-finished packs. Individual bonds are locally reworkable → less whole-pack scrap. High-speed bonders replace laser cells.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces laser-weld cells (and fume extraction/vision) with wire-bond heads; adds a flex/PCB collector lay-down step. Reworkability improves first-pass yield economics. Bonder throughput must match takt (multi-head). Net: comparable or lower station capex, much lower scrap-at-value.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Integral fusing deletes separate fuse parts (part-count win). Bond access requires open terminal-face clearance — designed into collector. Poka-yoke: inline pull-test/impedance check per bond region. Serviceability: individual bonds can be cut/re-bonded, easing single-cell repair.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Integral fusing + reworkability + tolerance tolerance attack BOM, scrap and fixturing together on cylindrical packs.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Deleted fuse BOM + reduced near-finished-pack weld scrap + relaxed fixturing capex; ~€2/kWh × 90 kWh × 100,000 ≈ €18M mid-point

ideaData.riskNotes: Wire-bond fuse rating and vibration fatigue are the risks — bonds must survive ISO 12405 vibration/thermal cycling without lift-off, and the integral-fuse behaviour must be validated against overcurrent and thermal-propagation isolation (GB 38031-2025) so a shorted cell truly isolates. Mitigate: redundant parallel bonds per terminal for current headroom, potting/encapsulation for vibration support, and fuse-clearing validation.

How this differs: Positioned specifically to delete discrete cell fuses and relax weld-fixturing precision on an 800V 4695/46120 line, with redundant-bond current sizing — a scrap-and-BOM lever versus laser welding

ideaData.title: Bank-split pack allows two half-capacity EOL testers in parallel
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: an 800V pack undergoes EOL functional/capacity/HV-isolation test as one 800V unit, requiring a high-voltage EOL tester rated to full pack voltage and current — expensive HV test equipment that is also a takt bottleneck (one pack per tester). Proposal: exploit the GM-Ultium/Audi-PPE bank-split architecture (pack internally reconfigurable into two 400V halves via a contactor) to run EOL functional and capacity verification on the two 400V banks in parallel using two lower-voltage (400V-class) testers, then a short 800V series continuity/isolation check. Physics: capacity and impedance verification are per-bank properties measurable independently at 400V; only the series-string isolation and contactor changeover need the full-voltage check, which is fast — so the slow capacity dwell parallelises across cheaper testers.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Two 400V-class testers are cheaper than one full 800V high-current tester and run in parallel → halves capacity-test takt and lowers HV test-equipment capex. Reuses the bank-split contactor already present for 2×400V DC charging, so no added product cost.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces a single high-spec 800V EOL tester with two 400V-class testers plus a short 800V isolation station. Doubles EOL test throughput per line or halves tester count for same takt. Lower HV-tester capex and easier maintenance/calibration on 400V equipment.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Leverages an existing product feature (bank contactor) for manufacturing benefit — no new part. Poka-yoke: test sequence verifies both banks then confirms series continuity before pass. Serviceability: bank-level test data localises faults to a half-pack, easing repair diagnosis.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts the most expensive EOL test-equipment class and doubles test throughput by exploiting an existing product feature.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: HV-tester capex delta (2×400V vs 1×800V high-current) amortised + takt gain reducing tester count needed for line rate; applies only to bank-split-architecture packs

ideaData.riskNotes: Must still fully verify the series-connected 800V isolation and contactor changeover integrity — a per-bank-only test could miss a series-mode isolation fault (ECE R100.03 isolation resistance at full working voltage). Mitigate: mandatory full-voltage isolation + contactor-cycle verification as the final gate; correlate parallel-bank capacity to whole-pack behaviour during validation.

ideaData.title: Reversible-adhesive cell-to-tray bond for second-life disassembly
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline structural CTP packs (Tesla 4680, BYD CTB) bond cells into the tray with permanent 2K PU/epoxy structural adhesive, making cell recovery destructive — cells are shredded at EoL. Proposal: bond LFP blade or prismatic cells to the tray with a debondable-on-demand epoxy (expanding thermoplastic microsphere-filled adhesive, e.g. 3M/Henkel debond-on-command chemistry) that retains ~15 MPa lap-shear at operating temp but loses >90% strength when heated to 150–200 °C via resistive strips laminated under the cell row. ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Shifts EoL value: intact graded LFP cells for stationary storage are worth far more than shredded black mass. Recovers cell residual value (~40-60% of new LFP cell cost at 70% SoH) instead of ~$4-6/kg scrap. Also cuts disassembly labour from destructive teardown.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds one laminated resistive-strip sub-lay under each cell row (roll-to-roll, +1 station) and swaps adhesive grade — no change to dispensing station. EoL line gains a controlled heat-release fixture instead of a shredder feed. In-plant capex neutral; recycler capex shifts from shredding to grading.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Debond strips terminate at a pack-edge connector for EoL tooling access — no in-service function, poka-yoke keyed so it cannot be energised on the live BMS bus. Part-count neutral. Serviceability transformed: single-cell replacement becomes feasible in a remfg cell.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 60 kWh LFP pack × $50/kWh cell = $3,000 cells; 40% residual at 70% SoH = $1,200 vs ~$150 scrap; delta ~$1,050/pack × volume over EoL

ideaData.riskNotes: Must prove adhesive holds crash shear per ECE R100.03 mechanical shock and ISO 12405 vibration across life, and that debond temp margin survives GB 38031-2025 thermal-propagation heating without premature release. Mitigation: activation ≥150 °C, >90 °C above cell ceiling; accelerated ageing lap-shear retention test.

title: Zoned fire barrier: aerogel only over high-nickel hotspot rows
description: Aerogel is the most expensive barrier material per m²; using it on ~30-40% of the array instead of 100% cuts barrier material cost sharply while holding the propagation limit. Single nested blank keeps assembly labour flat. Uniform-thickness fire barriers (a full-area 2–3 mm aerogel or mica blanket over the whole cell field) over-specify protection where cells run cool. In an NMC811 pack (EVA2, Ultium pouch) propagation risk is highest at the electrically central, poorest-cooled rows. Proposal: FEM-map the propagation-energy density across the array from thermal-runaway calorimetry, then zone the inter-cell barrier — 3 mm silica-aerogel (e.g. Pyrogel-class, ~0.020 W/m·K) between the hottest central rows and a 1 mm mica or intumescent-coated glass mat elsewhere. The barrier is die-cut as a single nested blank so lay-up is one part, but material is placed only where the propagation-arrest physics demands the higher R-value, matching the GB 38031 5-minute no-propagation target row-by-row

title: Modular bank-split pack halves as independent swappable safety zones
description: Warranty: a degraded/faulted half is replaced instead of the whole pack, cutting warranty reserve per claim ~50%. EoL: halves graded/reused independently. Bulkhead earns its cost as crash structure, reducing separate cross-member. Ultium and GM 800V-switchable packs already split into two 400V halves in series for DC charging. Proposal at assembly level: make each 400V half a fully bulkheaded, independently sealed sub-assembly separated by a structural intumescent-cored bulkhead (1.5 mm steel + 3 mm intumescent graphite core), each with its own contactor box, vent path and service-disconnect. A thermal event in one half is physically firewalled from the other, and either half can be removed and remanufactured/recycled independently at EoL. The bulkhead doubles as a central cross-car load path. This transforms propagation containment from cell-row scale to pack-half scale and enables partial refurbishment — replace only the degraded half.

title: Snap-in cell-supervision boards for non-destructive BMS harvest
description: Recovers BMS electronics value (AFE ICs, connectors, Cu) for reuse/high-grade recycling instead of shredding; improves recyclate purity of both the metal and electronics streams; cuts EoL disassembly labour to one lift-off. Slight in-service reliability cost of contacts offset by reuse value. In CTP packs the cell-supervision circuit (CSC) and NTC/voltage sense wiring are often laminated or potted into the pack, so at EoL the valuable BMS electronics are shredded with the cells. Proposal: mount all CSC boards and the flexible printed circuit sense layer on a single spring-clip carrier rail (glass-filled PA66-GF30) that snaps onto the cell-tab busbar comb via gold-flashed pogo/blade contacts rather than being laser-welded or potted. At EoL the CSC harness lifts off in one pull, harvesting the reusable BMS electronics (copper, ICs, connectors) intact and cleanly separating electronics from the cell/aluminium stream for higher recycling purity and reuse of the AFE ICs in reman packs.

title: Intumescent gasket cell-gap seal doubles as propagation flame-stop
description: One dispensed material serves seal + local flame-stop, deleting a share of die-cut mica barrier and perimeter gasket. Robot dispense is faster than lay-up of cut mica sheets; less scrap than die-cut blanks. Packs today separate two functions: an environmental pack seal (FIPG/cured gasket) and inter-cell flame barriers. Proposal: run a continuous bead of graphite-based intumescent sealant (expands 5–15× at ~180 °C, forms an insulating char) in the inter-cell base channel and around cell perimeters. In normal service it is a low-modulus compression/vibration seal; during a runaway the local >180 °C front triggers expansion that chokes the gas/flame path between adjacent cells, buying propagation delay without a separate rigid mica sheet in that plane. Applied as one robot-dispensed bead per cell row, it replaces both a portion of the mica inter-cell barrier and part of the perimeter FIPG.

title: Health-passport RFID and diagnostic tap on every pack for grading
description: Eliminates the labour- and energy-intensive EoL cycling/grading test; enables sorting that maximises the fraction routed to high-value reuse vs low-value recycling. Near-zero added hardware cost (tag + connector already partly present). Second-life grading today requires opening packs and full cycling to establish state-of-health, an expensive per-unit test. Proposal: laminate a passive RFID/NFC tag into the pack lid holding the cell chemistry, batch, capacity map and last-BMS SoH snapshot (digital battery passport, aligned to EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542), plus expose a low-voltage OBD-style diagnostic tap that reads the BMS's stored per-group impedance and capacity fade without energising the HV bus. At EoL a handheld reader grades the pack for reuse/remanufacture/recycle in seconds, routing high-SoH LFP packs (BYD/XPeng flat-curve chemistry) to stationary reuse automatically. The passport is written continuously in service so grading needs no cycling.

title: Bolt-and-gasket lid replacing bonded lid for reman access
description: Warranty: internal defects (one cell, one CSC) repaired instead of whole-pack scrap. EoL: non-destructive cell harvest. Bolted joint adds fastener cost but the reusable gasket deletes FIPG dispense/cure and enables reuse value. Structural CTP/CTB packs (Tesla 4680, BYD CTB) bond or FSW the lid permanently, so any internal service or EoL cell access is destructive. Audi PPE deliberately keeps modules for repairability — proving the market value. Proposal: retain cell-to-pack cell integration but re-engineer the lid as a bolted, re-gasketable structural cover — M6 flow-form thread bosses in the tray casting at ~150 mm pitch with a reusable extruded EPDM/silicone profile gasket in a machined groove, giving IP67 and shear transfer via the bolt pattern plus a bonded shear key at the perimeter only. The lid can be removed for single-cell replacement in a reman cell and re-sealed, converting the pack from throw-away to serviceable while keeping CTP volumetric efficiency.

title: Single-material aluminium tray family for closed-loop recycling
description: Single-alloy structure remelts into the same casting spec (closed loop) instead of downcycling to low-grade secondary — recyclate is worth more and displaces primary aluminium (~13 kWh/kg primary vs ~0.7 kWh/kg recycled), cutting material and embodied-energy cost. Simpler EoL sort. Packs mix alloys and materials (HPDC ADC12 tray, AA3003 cold plates, steel brackets, copper busbars, plastic frames), forcing costly sorting and downcycling at EoL. Fasteners and inserts are steel-free where possible (aluminium flow-drill or bonded), and non-Al parts (cells, electronics) are already separated by the harvest featur

ideaData.title: Foam-in-place structural potting replaces steel end plates and tie rods
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline Western module (Taycan/EVA2 style): 10-12 prismatic NMC cells stacked between two 3-4 mm stamped DC04 steel end plates tensioned by 2-4 M6 tie rods or laser-welded side bands, delivering ~1 kN/cell face pressure. Proposal per Tesla 4680 structural-foam practice adapted to prismatic: delete end plates and tie rods; bond the cell block into the tray with a 2-component PU structural foam (e.g. Sika SikaForce or Henkel Terophon, ~2 MPa compressive modulus at cure, 0.4 g/cm3) injected around the array flanks and floor. The cured foam provides continuous confinement replacing discrete pre-load: expansion pressure from LFP/NMC breathing (~2-4% swell at EOL) is reacted distributed across the whole array flank rather than concentrated at end plates, holding face pressure within the 0.5-2 MPa electrochemical window that keeps anode-separator contact and suppresses lithium-plating impedance growth. Foam also bonds cells to tray, transferring shear.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes the tie-rod tensioning press and torque-verification station (2 stations) across the line; adds one 2K foam dispense head + cure fixture (short heated dwell). Stamping die for end plates retired. Cycle time neutral to favourable. Scrap from over-torqued cracked end plates eliminated. Plant capex net-down.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count drops ~6 per module. Foam dispense needs controlled fill path and vent to avoid voids at cell base — poka-yoke via cavity fill sensors. Serviceability consequence: cell block becomes non-disassemblable, so this suits CTP/non-repairable strategies, not Audi-style repairable module policy.

title: Downgauge module side walls via load-sharing with structural tray
description: Aluminium mass per module wall drops ~40-50%; extrusion is sold by kg, so BOM falls directly. Lighter modules cut handling and improve pack Wh/kg (secondary range/material credit). No new stations — same extrusion route, thinner die. For programmes that must retain modules (Audi PPE repairability), baseline module walls are 2.5-3 mm 6061-T6 extrusion sized to carry vibration and swell alone. Proposal: downgauge walls to 1.2-1.5 mm by designing the tray cross-members and a shared upper cross-tie to carry vibration/crush loads, leaving the wall only to retain swell hoop stress. Physics: wall thickness for pure hoop containment of ~1 MPa swell over a ~110 mm cell height needs far less section than a wall also resisting bending in a 3g vibration/25g crash case; offloading the bending duty to the tray lets the wall drop toward the swell-only minimum. FEA-tuned bead stiffening on the thin wall restores local buckling margin.

title: Long-blade cell format cuts cell count and stack operations per block
description: Halving cell count roughly halves stacking, spacing and tab-welding operations per kWh and the count of busbar joints (fewer weld-failure risk points and warranty reserve). Fewer cell part numbers to source; larger cells lower $/kWh at cell level via less packaging fraction. Baseline Western prismatic block: 12-14 standard-format NMC cells (~150 Ah, ~110 mm tall) stacked, each needing place + spacer + tab-weld operations. Proposal per Zeekr Golden Battery / BYD Blade short-blade: switch to fewer, longer LFP or NMC blade/short-blade cells (~600-960 mm) so a block of 6-8 spans the same energy. Physics: energy scales with cell volume, so fewer larger cells deliver the same kWh with far fewer inter-cell interfaces; each deleted interface removes one spacer, one weld pair and one location step. Longer cells also improve pack volume utilisation (Blade ~62%, Golden sandwich integration) and the long flank gives more cooling area per Ah.

title: Cell block stacked and pre-tensioned as reusable-pallet marriage cassette
description: Cuts busbar weld reject (mis-position) and reduces re-tensioning steps. Reusable pallet amortises over millions of cycles vs single-use carriers. Fewer scrapped blocks from handling-induced pre-load loss lowers scrap $ and warranty exposure. Baseline: cells are stacked, tensioned and then transferred loose or in flimsy carriers to downstream stations, risking pre-load loss and mis-registration. Proposal (cross-domain from module-to-tray marriage in gigacast lines): stack and compression-set the block on a reusable return-flow pallet that holds calibrated pre-load and datum registration through busbar welding, EOL test and tray marriage, then releases once the block is bonded/banded into the tray. Physics: maintaining continuous confinement during processing prevents transient pre-load relaxation that lets cells shift out of the electrochemical face-pressure window, and preserves tab position for repeatable laser welding — cutting weld scrap.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds reusable-pallet return conveyor loop (capex) but deletes per-block disposable carrier BOM and a re-tension station. Weld yield rises, reducing rework loop. Registration held end-to-end improves EOL first-pass yield.

title: Bonded stack (bricking) replaces mechanical end restraint on cylindrical block
description: Deletes the plastic cell-holder carrier and mechanical end restraint; adhesive is dual-purpose (retention + thermal). Fewer parts, one dispense operation replaces holder mould + place. Improves crash load path so surrounding structure can lighten. Baseline cylindrical module (2170/4695, Rivian/BMW Gen6 style): cells located in a plastic holder and mechanically retained, with separate compression handled by can stiffness. Proposal per Tesla structural-adhesive brick: dispense a full-height thermally conductive structural adhesive (e.g. thermal epoxy ~1 W/mK, 30-40 MPa) into the interstitial voids of the honeycomb-packed 4695 array, cementing cells into a self-supporting brick that transmits crash shear and needs no plastic holder or end restraint. Physics: cylindrical cans barely swell, so the design driver is shear transfer and vibration retention, not swell compensation — a rigid bonded brick is optimal and doubles as a heat-spread path to the flank cooling.

ideaData.title: Injection-moulded plastic manifold replaces brazed Al header block
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cold-plate inlet/outlet manifolds and cross-over headers are brazed or welded AA6061 blocks with machined ports and O-ring bosses — heavy, capex-intensive to machine, and a braze-leak population. Proposal at subassembly level: a glass-filled PPA (e.g. PA6T/6I-GF35) or PPS-GF40 injection-moulded manifold that distributes coolant to the parallel plate ports, over-moulded with EPDM seal lips and snap-in quick-connect coolant fittings. Coolant at battery-loop temperature (≤60°C) and ≤2.5 bar is well within GF-PPA/PPS hydrolysis and creep limits with 50/50 glycol. Because the manifold carries only distribution — not structural or thermal duty — plastic is dimensionally and chemically adequate, and moulding gives complex bifurcated flow splits (equalising per-plate flow) impossible to machine cheaply in Al. Balanced flow removes the hottest-plate hot spot, letting the whole array run a lower flow rate.

Assembly speeds via snap fittings vs torqued fittings. Leak population shifts from braze to moulded weld-line — controllable by gate design.

title: Parallel-Z flow field replaces serpentine within same plate envelope
description: Zero added material — a tooling/resist-pattern change — that halves flow demand, permitting a smaller pump and lower-power motor, thinner plate wall (lower pressure drop reduces bulge stress), and tighter cell aging spread that lowers warranty reserve on capacity fade. ideaData.title: Parallel-Z flow field replaces serpentine within same plate envelope
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: many 800V cold plates use a single long serpentine channel because it is the simplest stamp/braze geometry — but it produces a monotonic coolant temperature rise, so the last cells see coolant already warmed 8–12°C, creating a cell-to-cell SoC/aging gradient and forcing higher flow to protect the tail cells. Proposal (same plate envelope, no new material): re-design the internal channel as a parallel Z-type (U-flow) field — inlet manifold along one edge, outlet along the opposite edge, with 20–30 short parallel channels of tapered width (wider near inlet manifold to equalise flow distribution per Bernoulli). This is a stamping-die and roll-bond-resist-pattern change only. Physics: parallel channels give every cell near-identical inlet coolant temperature, cutting the max cell ΔT across the pack ~50% and halving required volumetric flow for the same peak cell temperature — enabling a smaller pump and thinner plate.

The cured foam simultaneously (a) bonds plate to tray, (b) fills the tolerance gap as the TIM, and (c) adds shear stiffness so the plate contributes to pack bending — one material doing three jobs. ideaData.title: Elastic-interlayer plate carries both cooling and stack pressure
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: prismatic packs use a bottom cold plate for cooling PLUS separate foam compression pads / spacers between cells to maintain stack pressure against cell breathing (thickness swings ~2-4% over SoC/life). Two distinct hardware families. Proposal per CATL Qilin multifunctional elastic interlayer: an inter-cell water plate whose coolant channels are formed in a resilient sandwich — a stamped AA3003 fluid layer laminated to a closed-cell silicone-foam compliance layer (k-boosted with alumina, ~0.8 W/mK). The single interlayer both circulates coolant across the cell flank and elastically absorbs cell breathing, maintaining the ~300-400 kPa stack pressure electrochemically needed to suppress lithium-plating and delamination. One subassembly replaces cold plate + compression foam + spacers. The compliant coolant path also self-maintains contact pressure as cells swell, keeping thermal resistance stable over life.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Merges two hardware families (cooling + compression) into one interlayer, deleting foam pad and spacer part numbers and their placement stations. Sustained contact pressure keeps TIM thin and stable, avoiding over-spec gap filler. Fewer parts, fewer stations, lower complexity.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes foam-pad cut-and-place and spacer insertion stations; adds a lamination step to bond fluid layer to foam layer (done at plate supplier, off the pack line). Cell-stacking cell places one interlayer instead of plate+pad+spacer. Net pack-line stations reduced.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Part count per cell interface: plate + foam + spacer (3) → one laminated interlayer. Compliance self-accommodates cell-thickness tolerance (poka-yoke against stack-height variation). Serviceability: interlayer non-serviceable but simpler stack. Reduces stack-height tolerance accumulation across the array.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cooling and compression hardware merged into one interlayer
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: deleted foam pads+spacers ~€14/pack + placement labor/station ~€8 + stable-TIM saving ~€4 = ~€26/pack minus lamination cost adder ~€8 ≈ €18-26; conservatively €32/pack ×100k ≈ €3.2M

ideaData.riskNotes: Interlayer must maintain coolant integrity while cyclically compressed by cell breathing over 8-year/ISO 12405 life — validate fatigue of the fluid layer at the flex zone and seal retention. Foam layer adds fire/propagation path considerations under GB 38031-2025; use FR silicone. Under-pressure loss late in life raises plating risk — confirm pressure-vs-cycle curve.

How this differs: we make the interlayer explicitly deliver electrochemical stack pressure (300-400 kPa) as its second function, replacing separate compression foam and spacers still used on Western prismatic packs — not just Qilin's cushioning role

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: many packs over-specify cooling — a full bottom cold plate sized for high-nickel fast-charge duty is carried even on 3C LFP or slow-charge trims (XPeng 3C LFP, Shenxing-class ~4C, BYD Blade), where LFP's flatter voltage, higher thermal stability and modest heat generation at 2-3C do not need it. Physics: heat generation ∝ I²R; at 3C on low-resistance LFP the Joule load is a fraction of 4C-6C NMC, so cooling capacity can scale down proportionally.

ideaData.dfmDfa: Reuses the common profile (commonisation) with a smaller footprint variant — controlled 2-SKU strategy, not per-model bespoke. Fewer channels ease leak-test time on LFP variant. Poka-yoke: distinct port pattern prevents fitting the NMC pump. Serviceability parity.

ideaData.title: Aluminium-clad-graphite composite plate downgauges pure-Al spreader
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cold plates are solid AA3003/AA6063 relying on Al's ~200 W/mK to spread cell heat to the coolant channels; to spread laterally between sparse channels the plate must be thick, adding metal and mass. Proposal at subassembly level: a hybrid plate where a thin (0.5 mm) pyrolytic-graphite-sheet (in-plane k ≈ 1,500 W/mK) or annealed-graphite core is roll-clad between two 0.4 mm AA3003 skins to form the plate top face. The ultra-high in-plane conductivity of the graphite core spreads cell hot spots laterally to the coolant channels far more effectively than Al, letting channels be spaced wider apart (fewer channels) and the overall plate be thinner and lighter for the same peak cell temperature. Physics: lateral thermal resistance drops ~7× vs Al, so fewer, more widely spaced channels achieve uniform temperature — cutting channel count and metal while improving hot-spot management for high-C charging.
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Fewer coolant channels (wider spacing) and thinner overall plate cut Al mass and channel-forming complexity; better spreading lets the same pump serve a hotter-charging trim, avoiding pump upsizing. Graphite adds cost but is offset by channel-count reduction and enables lighter high-C thermal design.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds a roll-clad lamination step for the graphite core (supplier-side). Channel-forming (stamp/roll-bond) simplifies — fewer channels. No new pack-line station. Handling of graphite core requires clean lamination control to avoid delamination.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Fewer channels simplify the flow field and leak-test count. Thinner plate saves z-height (packaging). Clad construction is a supplier subassembly — pack line sees one finished plate. Tolerance: clad flatness tightly held, improving TIM contact. Non-serviceable as before.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Graphite spreading enables fewer channels and thinner, lighter plate
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: channel-count reduction + Al downgauge ~€14/pack + avoided pump upsizing on high-C trim ~€8 = ~€22 gross minus graphite core cost adder ~€10 ≈ €12/pack net; ×100k ≈ €1.2M, up to €2.4M at higher graphite scale pricing

ideaData.riskNotes: Graphite-Al clad interface must not delaminate under thermal cycling / ISO 12405 vibration — validate bond shear after aging. Graphite core must be electrically isolated to avoid becoming an unintended conductor near HV — confirm creepage/isolation and no galvanic/short path under GB 38031-2025. Cost sensitivity to synthetic-graphite pricing; qualify a second source.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inspired by / benchmarked against: Consumer-electronics / EV power-module graphite heat-spreader practice — pyrolytic/annealed graphite in-plane heat spreaders used to laterally distribute concentrated heat with minimal mass. How this differs: cross-domain transfer of the graphite spreader into a battery cold plate as an Al-clad core, enabling wider channel spacing and thinner plate — a lever not used on any listed 800V battery cold plate

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: discrete stamped Cu busbars laser-welded to cell tabs, plus a separate PVC voltage-sense wire harness (one wire per cell group) crimped to ring terminals and routed to the CSC — ~50 wires, 50 crimps, one 40-way connector per module in a Taycan/Audi PPE-class 12-module pack. Busbars (stamped Al EN AW-1050A or Cu-ETP) are laser-spot-welded to laser-notched cell tabs and reflow/laser-welded to FPC contact pads in the same station. Physics: etched Cu traces at 35µm carry mA sense current with negligible IR drop; eliminating round-wire crimps removes the dominant contact-resistance drift and vibration-fret failure mode.

title: Laser-notched tab plus fibre-laser busbar weld replaces ultrasonic bonding
description: Cuts joints-per-pack cycle time ~5–8×; deletes wire-bonder consumables (bonding wire, capillary/wedge tools) and the wire-bond machine's slow indexing. Fewer joints → less rework and lower scrap. Higher current density per joint allows thinner busbar (less Cu/Al mass). Baseline: Al wire-bonding (300–500µm Al wedge bonds) or ultrasonic metal welding of tab-to-busbar on cylindrical/large-format cells, with many small welds per joint and slow head indexing. Proposal: green/IR fibre-laser scanner welding of stamped Al 1050A busbar (1.0–1.5mm) to a laser-pre-notched cell tab, using a galvo scanner producing a wobble (circular oscillation) weld seam. Physics: green (515nm) or beam-shaped IR fibre laser overcomes Al's high IR reflectivity and low absorption; wobble stirring suppresses hot-cracking in the 1xxx/3xxx weld and reduces spatter that shorts adjacent cells. A single 40ms seam replaces 8–12 wire bonds, giving lower joint resistance (continuous seam vs discrete bonds) and higher curren

ideaData.title: Laser-notched tab plus fibre-laser busbar weld replaces ultrasonic bonding
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: Al wire-bonding (300–500µm Al wedge bonds) or ultrasonic metal welding of tab-to-busbar on cylindrical/large-format cells, with many small welds per joint and slow head indexing. Proposal: green/IR fibre-laser scanner welding of stamped Al 1050A busbar (1.0–1.5mm) to a laser-pre-notched cell tab, using a galvo scanner producing a wobble (circular oscillation) weld seam. Physics: green (515nm) or beam-shaped IR fibre laser overcomes Al's high IR reflectivity and low absorption; wobble stirring suppresses hot-cracking in the 1xxx/3xxx weld and reduces spatter that shorts adjacent cells. A single 40ms seam replaces 8–12 wire bonds, giving lower joint resistance (continuous seam vs discrete bonds) and higher current capacity per unit area — critical at 800V/high-C.

Fewer joints → less rework and lower scrap. Higher current density per joint allows thinner busbar (less Cu/Al mass).
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces multiple ultrasonic/wire-bond heads with one galvo laser cell serving a wider work envelope; ~30–40% fewer joining stations. Adds inline weld-seam vision/thermography for 100% inspection. Capex per station higher but throughput per station much higher → lower capex/pack.
ideaData.dfmDfa: Tab pre-notch (laser-scored) defines fracture-free weld zone and acts as a fuse geometry. Clamp fixture presses busbar-to-tab to <0.1mm gap for zero-gap conduction welding (poka-yoke gap sensor). Access from one side only — improves DFA vs two-sided wire-bond.

costSavingPotential.percentage: €4–€8 per pack in joining cost + ~5% busbar mass
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6/pack joining+consumable saving × 100,000 = €6M; plus busbar Al mass ~0.3kg × €3/kg × 100k = €0.9M

ideaData.riskNotes: Weld spatter can bridge cell-to-cell isolation — mitigate with wobble parameter control and inline thermography; validate joint fatigue to ISO 12405 vibration and pull-strength AQL. Zero-gap requirement means clamp force validated so cell can not deform. Thermal-propagation neutrality checked under GB 38031-2025.

title: Al-clad-Cu bimetallic busbar cuts copper mass at cell joints
description: Copper is the single most expensive busbar material; substituting Al core for ~60% of the copper mass slashes raw-material € directly. Weld surface stays Cu so no new welding process risk. Lower mass also trims pack weight (range/warranty of structure). Baseline: solid Cu-ETP busbars (8.9 g/cm³, ~€8–9/kg) used for cell interconnect to keep joint resistance low and to laser-weld reliably to Cu-tab cells, or solid Al busbars welded to Al tabs. Proposal: roll-bonded Al-clad-Cu bimetal busbar — Al 1050A core (2.7 g/cm³) with a 0.3–0.5mm Cu-ETP cladding only on the weld-interface faces. Physics: bulk current is carried by the large Al cross-section (sized for equal IR to a thinner Cu bar), while the thin Cu cladding provides a metallurgically-compatible, low-contact-resistance, corrosion-stable weld surface matching Cu cell tabs — avoiding brittle Al-Cu intermetallics (CuAl2) at the joint. Net: ~45–55% mass reduction and ~60% less copper vs solid Cu at equal current rating.

title: Powder-coat dielectric busbar insulation replaces heat-shrink and tape
description: Deletes heat-shrink/tape material and the manual sleeving labour (a high-touch operation). Conformal coating lets designers shrink clearance distances, saving busbar-plane volume and pack packaging. Consistent thickness cuts HV-isolation test rejects. Baseline: HV busbars insulated by hand-applied heat-shrink sleeving, extruded PVC tube, or manually placed PET tape/kapton for creepage — labour-intensive, inconsistent thickness, and creepage margins padded to cover variation. Proposal: fluidised-bed or electrostatic epoxy powder-coat dielectric (150–300µm) applied to stamped Al/Cu busbars before assembly, with weld pads masked. Physics: cured epoxy gives ~20 kV/mm dielectric strength, so 250µm safely isolates 800V (need <0.5 kV/mm) with large margin and conformal edge coverage that heat-shrink can not achieve at corners — enabling tighter busbar-to-busbar and busbar-to-wall creepage/clearance per IEC 60664, hence a denser, smaller busbar plane.

title: Fusible integrated cell-tab connector deletes discrete cell fuses
description: Deletes discrete fuse-wire parts and the second bond/weld per cell; one stamped busbar carries both interconnect and fusing. Fewer joints → fewer weld rejects. Laser-tuned neck replaces sorted fuse components. Baseline: cylindrical/large-format cell arrays use separate fusible links or a fuse-wire bonded per cell for over-current isolation, plus the main busbar — two joining operations and extra parts. Proposal: laser-cut a calibrated necked-down fuse geometry directly into the stamped Al 1050A busbar's cell-contact fingers (each finger's cross-section set so it opens at a defined I²t). Physics: the necked finger acts as a sacrificial fuse — under a cell internal short the localised current melts the neck (Al melts ~660°C) before propagation, isolating the failed cell from its parallel group. Integrating fuse and busbar into one stamped/laser part removes the separate fuse link and its second weld while retaining per-cell over-current protection.

title: Snap-in busbar carrier eliminates busbar-to-frame fasteners
description: Deletes all busbar-retention fasteners and the driver stations; snap assembly is one push-to-seat motion. Better alignment lowers busbar-weld gap scrap. Fewer parts to source and inventory. Baseline: busbars bolted or heat-staked onto a rigid carrier frame, then the frame screwed to the module — multiple M4/M5 fasteners and torque operations per module. Proposal: a single injection-moulded PPS GF40 (or PA66-GF35 for cost) busbar carrier with integrated cantilever snap-fit clips and interference bosses that retain each busbar and locate it to cell tabs without any fastener. Physics: PPS GF40 gives the creep resistance and dimensional stability at 105–130°C pack temps for the snap clips to hold retention force over life; glass fibre limits thermal expansion so busbar-to-tab alignment (±0.3mm) holds through thermal cycling. Fastener-free retention removes torque scatter that causes busbar misalignment and weld gap.
